name: Ningyocho
tagline: Otemachi in 4 minutes and Tokyo in 9 minutes. Served by 3 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000.
summary: The station is in Chuo City, where Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 3 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 4 minutes to Otemachi, 25 minutes to Shinjuku, 23 minutes to Shibuya and 19 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. The station stands 2.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.3 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 2.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.6 m to 3.9 m, a difference of 2.3 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 9 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 6 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 12 clinics and 8 pharmacies. The nearest facility recorded as a hospital is 山村病院, about 671 m from the station. The next nearest is いしせ脳神経外科クリニック, about 1346 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 3 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line also call here. Toei Asakusa Line are available too. The lines are split between operators (Tokyo Metro runs 2 lines and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line runs at 163% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 三ノ輪→入谷, which this station is not on. Toei Asakusa Line runs at 123%. Its busiest stretch is 本所吾妻橋→浅草, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line runs at 111%. Its busiest stretch is 渋谷→表参道, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: One room ¥130,000 to ¥140,000, 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000, 1LDK ¥210,000 to ¥220,000 and 2LDK ¥280,000 to ¥290,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Ningyocho is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: 579 m away in a straight line. It takes 11 minutes longer to reach Otemachi than Ningyocho. One-room rents run about ¥5,000 lower.

neighbours.lead: Kayabacho is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Ningyocho is ahead on the number of lines and how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: 665 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Ningyocho. One-room rents run about ¥5,000 higher.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want another route when a line stops
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: The 首都高速6号向島線 viaduct runs 371 m away. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
新大橋通り (4 lanes each way) runs 170 m away. Traffic on it never stops

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 13 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, comparatively many of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 3 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the lowest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are some of the most heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
